Incorporating the January 2018 SLOOS into the FOMC’s March 2018 statement assessment, the near-term macro tone is modestly more supportive. Banks reported easing in C&I standards and terms, particularly for large and middle‑market firms, with narrower loan rate spreads and competition as a key driver; some banks also expected to ease standards for small firms and saw potential quality improvement in nonsyndicated loans. These signals point to a still-accommodative credit backdrop consistent with continued job gains and moderate growth. Offsetting this, banks tightened standards and noted weaker demand in CRE (especially construction and land development), and consumer credit showed mixed-to-softer signs, including expectations of performance deterioration in credit cards and HELOCs and some anticipated tightening. Netting these dynamics with the FSR lens (elevated valuations and corporate leverage risks), the SLOOS tilts the balance slightly more positive for near-term activity but keeps a prudent, gradual policy path appropriate.
